title: Strip a 14 AWG wire to a receptacle's strip gauge and push it into the hot-side push-in hole
instruction: Strip the black wire to the receptacle's 5/8 inch (16 mm) strip gauge with the wire stripper, then push it fully into a push-in hole on the brass (hot) side of the receptacle's back, and let go of it.
context: Every conductor an electrician connects is first stripped to the length its terminal calls for: in O*NET 31.0, 73% of electricians (818,700 US jobs in 2024) report connecting wires to breakers and other components daily or more. The strip must be the gauge's length, unnicked, and the hot conductor must land on the brass side.
setup: Station table, two YAM arms; positions are (x forward from the arm bases, y left) in cm, heights above the table top. Wire stripper (Klein 11055 pattern, 10-18 AWG solid): 181 mm, 154 g, steel jaws with stripping holes for 10, 12, 14, 16 and 18 AWG solid (the 14 AWG hole 26 mm from the pivot, larger holes nearer the pivot), straight blue and yellow vinyl-dipped handles, a return spring holding it open. It lies flat with its jaws open and pointing +x, pivot at (30.0, -10.0), 20.0 cm up, the jaws overhanging the front of a grey steel stand: one block 2.4 x 3.0 cm under the pivot (top 19.7 cm) at (29.4, -10.0) and one 1.2 x 7.0 cm under the handles (top 19.25 cm) at (23.0, -11.2). Wire: one 150 mm black pigtail of 14 AWG solid copper THHN/THWN-2 (1.63 mm conductor, 2.69 mm over the PVC and nylon jacket), standing end-up in a beech block 20 x 20 x 30 mm with a 4 mm square hole at (40.0, 4.0). Receptacle: a white 15 A duplex receptacle (Leviton T5320-W pattern; body 33 x 72 x 22 mm, steel strap 106 x 22 mm) held with its back facing down 18.5 cm above the table, centred at (45.0, -5.0), its length along y, on a grey 2 x 1 cm post, 20.7 cm tall, under the strap's -y end at (45.0, -10.0). Its four push-in holes (14 AWG solid only) are 11 mm either side of its centre in x and 10 mm either side in y: the brass-screw (hot) pair on the side facing the robot, at x 43.9, and the silver-screw (neutral) pair on the far side, at x 46.1. Both arms start in the ready pose with open grippers.
scoring: In simulation, at the end of the trial: 0 if the wire is in a push-in hole on the silver (neutral) side (reversed polarity), if it was nicked (closed in a smaller hole than 14 AWG) or cut between holes. Otherwise strip credit: 0.3 if the slug is fully off and the bare length is 14 to 18 mm, 0.15 if 12 to 20 mm, else 0. Termination, only with strip credit: 0.7 if the conductor is clamped in a brass-side push-in hole at least 12 mm deep, with at most 1.5 mm of copper showing between the jacket and the receptacle's back and the jacket no more than 1.5 mm inside the hole, and no fingertip within 8 mm of the wire. Success (1.0) when both hold for 1 s. Real trial, after the robot lets go: copper showing at the back by feeler or caliper (at most 1.5 mm); side by the screw colour; a 10 N tug on the wire for 5 s must not pull it out (the clamp is engaged); then release the wire with a 1/8 in screwdriver in the hole's release slot and measure the bare length by caliper and inspect the copper under a 10x loupe: any nick, ring or scrape in the copper scores 0.
reset_notes: Each trial uses a new 150 mm pigtail cut from the same reel. Release the previous wire from the push-in hole with a screwdriver in its release slot, and clear the cut slug from the stripper's jaws.
fidelity: Rigid bodies at 240 Hz. Wire: rigid copper core, last 50 mm of jacket as 2 mm rings (heavier than real). The cut is code: jaws within 2 degrees of shut on a hole turn off the rings at the blade; the hole decides clean, nicked or uncut. The slug holds by a 10 N/mm spring and comes off past 1 mm (10 N, a chosen value). Push-in clamp: a slide holding the wire at its deepest point from 12 mm. Simplified: boxy handles, U-notched jaws, square holes, stripper on a stand, no strip-gauge mark.
scores: Dream-1 run (dreamlabs/dream-1-beta, 2,400 steps): 0.0, the right hand went to the stripper and knocked it off its stand, and the wire was never stripped; scripted demo: 1.0 (978 steps).
